_help: The Harvest page (/harvest/) tracks Muslims leaving Islam and coming to Christ, as far as that can be counted.

channels: YouTube channels whose newest videos' comments are read each build for first-person testimonies ('I left Islam', 'I accepted Jesus'), and whose subscriber counts are shown as reach. Each needs a channelId (UC...). Keep it to channels that reach Muslims; every channel costs about 25 quota units a build.
figures: the scoreboard of published survey numbers. Give value, label, detail, source, url, date. Update when a new survey appears.
trends: Google Trends keywords (up to 3) and ISO country codes (up to 4) for the search-interest charts.
testimonyForm: a Google Form 'embed' URL (Form → Send → <> → copy the src) for readers to tell their story; leave empty to show a Telegram invitation instead.

figures.label: Christians in Iran, almost all converts
figures.detail: An anonymous online survey of about 50,000 Iranians found 1.5% calling themselves Christian, 22% with no religion and 9% atheist. Only a third still identified as Shia Muslims, in a country whose government reports 99% Muslim.

figures.label: Americans raised Muslim who no longer identify as Muslim
figures.detail: Where leaving costs nothing, about a quarter leave. Pew also finds converts into Islam roughly balance the losses in the United States.

figures.label: Arabs describing themselves as 'not religious'
figures.detail: Across ten Arab countries the share rose in six years, to about a third in Tunisia, with the sharpest change among the under-30s.
figures.source: Arab Barometer, reported by the BBC

figures.label: Iran's underground church
figures.detail: Open Doors ranks the Iranian church among the fastest-growing in the world, meeting in homes, fed by satellite television, Farsi Bibles and, in testimony after testimony, dreams of Jesus.

figures.label: More Muslims in 2020 than in 2010, almost all by birth
figures.detail: Islam is still the fastest-growing religion in numbers because Muslim families are young and large; Pew finds Muslims among the groups least likely to change religion where it can be measured, which is to say outside the countries where it is a crime.
figures.source: Pew Research Center, How the Global Religious Landscape Changed

figures.label: A Muslim cleric's own lament, never verified
figures.detail: In December 2000 the Libyan cleric Ahmad al-Qataani told Al Jazeera that six million African Muslims were becoming Christians every year. Nobody has substantiated the figure; it is quoted here as his alarm, not as a count.
